container: Nanotechnology offers ways to improve medicine, manufacturing, energy, and environmental protection. Tiny particles can deliver drugs directly to diseased cells, making treatments more effective and reducing side effects. Nanomaterials may create lighter, stronger products, more efficient batteries, and filters that remove pollutants from water. However, these benefits come with risks. Because nanoparticles are small, they may enter the body or ecosystems in unexpected ways. Their long term effects remain uncertain, and production can expose workers or release harmful materials. Responsible research, clear regulation, and monitoring are essential to ensure innovation protects people and the planet.
